result: notes only; no source change. Calibrated MIR frame-pin oracle (colour, interval and alloca levels) and the bound table of 27 bases. No skeleton-positive base beats main with any legal original-like frame.

oracle.colour_level: llc -stop-before=prologepilog; stack objects -> fixedStack at chosen offsets; -start-before=prologepilog; identity pin byte-identical
oracle.interval_level: llc -stop-before=stack-slot-coloring (one FI per spill interval); colmap pin reproduces the real build byte for byte on all 27 bases; legal sharing via debug-llc live ranges
oracle.alloca_level: llc -stop-before=stack-coloring; every IR alloca a fixed object; identity (StackColoring merge log) byte-identical
oracle.outgoing_arg_fix: MIR round trip prints stack-arg stores as [r10+X]; rewritten to [r10-(0x1000-X)]

findings: Frame-masked M is not a frame bound: e3+tu8 masked 2374 vs legal interval pin 2264; RAR+V1 masked +67 over main ties main (2255 vs 2256) with the original's frame
Unrealizable masked credit sits in per-access splits of single objects (alloca merges _112.i/_109.i, sk in the 0x518 group, holder_key) and alignment artifacts
Colour-level pins are ~65 M below interval pins: the frame gap is colouring, not slot order
Best single interval move on main +12 M; best pairwise colour swap 0x8d8<->0x8e0 (holder vs accounts pointer) +12 M (+0.0036)
Colour order = StackSlotColoring weight order (sum of block frequency of spill/reload instructions); on ours holder outweighs the accounts pointer
difflib ratio is non-monotone: more consistent frame accesses can lower the score (alloca pin 797->842 consistent, ratio 0.63481->0.62972)
attempts: 27 base bounds + hill + alloca + swap screen + 4 source holder variants (HV1 0.63122, HV2 byte-identical, HV1+HV2 = HV1, HV3 0.38871); 3 sk-lifetime variants (SK1 0.53426, SK2 0.54144, SK3 0.53977)
rejected_mechanisms: any skeleton base under a legal frame
sk bound early (shared test / before PDA / before CtoState)
